task.description: Hard gate: review PAR-01/02/03/04 against docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md. HIGH RISK: this batch restructures the core events table, adds a DROP-TABLE-capable retention/deletion mechanism (events_ephemeral), and retires an existing function (Store.archive()) that was ADP-11's (protected-event-type deletion prohibition) implementation. Check: (1) RetentionClassForbidden guard is genuinely enforced -- can a protected-family event type (INSTANCE_*/TASK_*/GATEWAY_*/EXECUTION_*) actually be routed to events_ephemeral (i.e. hard-deleted) through any path, bypassing the guard? Check both the app-level Registry.registerType() check AND whether Store.append()'s routing logic re-derives retention_class in a way that could diverge from what was validated at registration time. (2) The DROP TABLE mechanism in partition_retention.zig -- confirm it is CONFINED to events_ephemeral partitions only and cannot be tricked/misconfigured into dropping an events or events_archive partition (which would be irreversible data loss of non-ephemeral data). (3) SQL parameterization on all new queries, especially any dynamic partition-name construction (ALTER TABLE ... ATTACH/DETACH PARTITION, CREATE TABLE events_YYYY_MM) -- partition names are typically NOT bindable as SQL parameters (DDL doesn't support $1 placeholders for identifiers), so check how this project safely constructs these identifier strings (allowlist/format validation vs any risk of injection via a crafted event_type or tenant-controlled value influencing a partition name). (4) No catch unreachable on realistic DB failure paths, especially around the two bugs BACKEND-DEV found and fixed (schema-qualification issue, duplicate UUID generation) -- confirm the fixes are sound. (5) Cross-tenant isolation: does the partitioning scheme correctly apply per-tenant-schema (via search_path) the same way other per-tenant tables do, or could partition maintenance/retention operating cross-schema accidentally touch the wrong tenant's data?
acceptance_criteria: RetentionClassForbidden guard verified unbypassable for protected-family types
DROP TABLE mechanism verified confined to events_ephemeral only
SQL parameterization verified including dynamic partition-name construction
Cross-tenant isolation of partition maintenance/retention verified

result.summary:
Security review of PAR-01/02/03/04 (commit 60a17439) against all 8 invariants. APPLIES and SATISFIED: INV-1 (tenant isolation - lint_migration_schema.py and lint_sql_table_refs.py both 0 violations; new tables events/events_archive/events_ephemeral/plat_partition_catalog/plat_partition_maintenance_run_log/plat_event_idempotency all created unqualified, resolve per-schema via search_path, no public.<business_table> references), INV-6 (this review), INV-7 (SQL parameterization - lint_sql_param_types.py 0 findings; all dynamic DDL identifier construction uses std.fmt.allocPrint/EXECUTE format(%I,%L) with compile-time-fixed or server-computed calendar-derived strings, never tenant/user input - traced every allocPrint SQL builder in partition_attach.zig, partition_maintenance.zig, partition_retention.zig, store.zig), INV-8 (no catch unreachable on realistic failure paths - grep found exactly one new hit, partition_maintenance.zig:374's bufPrint into a fixed [7]u8 buffer with bounded 4-digit-year/2-digit-month format specifiers, genuinely unreachable, not I/O/tenant-input-dependent). NOT-APPLICABLE: INV-2 and INV-5 (no src/api/routes/** changes in this diff - purely event-store/DB-partitioning internals), INV-3 and INV-4 (no src/lua/host_api, src/wasm/host_api, or src/secrets/** touched). All 3 new zig build test steps (test-partition-attach, test-partition-maintenance, test-partition-retention) pass exit 0. Detailed findings for the 5 handoff-specified checks below.

CHECK 1 (RetentionClassForbidden unbypassable): CONFIRMED unbypassable via two independent layers. (a) App-level: registry.zig's validateRegisterParams() rejects retention_class='delete' for any name matching isProtectedEventFamilyName() (INSTANCE_/TASK_/GATEWAY_/EXECUTION_ prefix) before any DB write, called from registerType() as the first statement. (b) DB-level backstop: migration 1149's chk_retention_class_protected_family CHECK constraint enforces the identical rule server-side, independent of the app-level guard - so even a hypothetical app-level bypass would be caught at INSERT/UPDATE time. Traced Store.append()'s routing (store.zig:276-290): it does NOT re-derive retention_class from event_type at append time - it reads retention_class from registry.getType()'s DB row (the value actually persisted, validated at registration time by both guards above), so there is no window where append-time routing could diverge from what was validated at registration. target_table selection is a pure two-way literal-string branch on that fetched value, never influenced by user input directly. TC-ADP-11-02/TC-ADP-11-03 in event_store_integration_test.zig exercise both branches end-to-end against a real DB (non-protected delete-class routes to events_ephemeral and is genuinely dropped; protected-family row is archived via DETACH/ATTACH and stays queryable, never routed to events_ephemeral).

CHECK 2 (DROP TABLE confined to events_ephemeral): CONFIRMED confined. partition_retention.zig's runEphemeralDrop() selects drop candidates via 'SELECT table_name FROM plat_partition_catalog WHERE parent_table = ''events_ephemeral'' AND state = ''ATTACHED''' - parent_table is a hardcoded SQL literal, not a variable, so the query is structurally incapable of returning an events/events_archive-parented row. Traced every INSERT into plat_partition_catalog across the whole diff (migration 1149's seed loop and partition_maintenance.zig's ensurePartitionAttached()): parent_table values only ever come from the fixed compile-time array PROVISIONED_PARENTS=['events','events_ephemeral'] or migration-literal 'events'/'events_archive'/'events_ephemeral' strings - no code path writes an events_ephemeral-parented catalog row for a table that is actually an events/events_archive partition. The DROP TABLE {s} argument (table_name) is DB-read, traceable only to this closed set. Additionally gated by the ADP-11 pre-drop guard (COUNT(*) protected-family rows in the candidate partition must be 0) as defense in depth before the DROP executes, and by chk_retention_class_protected_family (CHECK 1) preventing protected-family rows from ever being routed there in the first place - two independent layers must both fail for a protected-family row to even exist in an events_ephemeral partition.

CHECK 3 (SQL parameterization / dynamic partition-name DDL): CONFIRMED safe. Every identifier interpolated into DDL text (CREATE TABLE/ATTACH/DETACH PARTITION/DROP TABLE/ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN) across migrations 1147/1149 and partition_attach.zig/partition_maintenance.zig/partition_retention.zig/store.zig is one of: (a) a migration-computed 'events'/'events_archive'/'events_ephemeral' + to_char(date,'YYYY_MM') string built via PostgreSQL's format(%I,...) (identifier-safe quoting, not string concatenation), (b) a Zig-side partition/table name built from the fixed PROVISIONED_PARENTS array plus a purely-arithmetic YYYY_MM suffix (never any string received from an API request or tenant-controlled column), or (c) a table_name read back from plat_partition_catalog, which per CHECK 2's trace can only ever contain the computed forms above. The one genuinely dynamic, DB-read identifier reuse is store.zig's duplicate-idempotency-key resolution path (line ~505), which builds 'SELECT ... FROM {s} WHERE event_id::text = $1' with table_name iterating over the fixed 3-element literal array ['events','events_ephemeral','events_archive'] - not from any row or external input. All literal values (range bounds, event payloads, idempotency keys) use $N placeholders throughout; grep for allocPrint-built SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE found zero hits (the allocPrint calls build DDL text or plain literal formatting, never DML with embedded values). lint_sql_param_types.py: 0 findings.

CHECK 4 (catch unreachable / BACKEND-DEV's two self-found fixes): Both fixes verified sound. Fix A (schema-qualification bug): migrations 1147/1149's partition-seeding DO blocks now scope every catalog existence check (pg_partitioned_table/pg_class/pg_inherits) with an explicit 'JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace AND n.nspname = current_schema()' predicate rather than a bare to_regclass()/unqualified relname match - this is the exact correct remedy documented in anti-patterns.md's 'Database - System Catalog Introspection' entry, and matches the pattern partition_attach.zig's verifyAttachConstraints() independently already used correctly (regclass-cast resolution, inherently schema-scoped by search_path, documented inline as such). Fix B (duplicate UUID generation): store.zig's append() now captures the event_id plat_event_idempotency's own INSERT generates (via RETURNING event_id) into generated_event_id and binds that SAME value explicitly as $10::uuid into the events/events_ephemeral INSERT, rather than letting that INSERT's own gen_random_uuid() column DEFAULT fire a second, independent time - correctly eliminating the two-different-UUIDs orphaning bug. No new catch unreachable introduced on any DB/I/O/tenant-input path; the sole new catch-unreachable hit (partition_maintenance.zig:374, monthRange()'s suffix bufPrint) is bounded pure arithmetic into a fixed-size buffer, genuinely unreachable.

CHECK 5 (cross-tenant isolation of partition maintenance/retention) - OBSERVATION, not a BLOCKER: PartitionMaintenanceScheduler.runMaintenanceCycle() and PartitionRetention.runArchivalAging()/runEphemeralDrop() call self.pool.acquire() directly with no tenant_context.set() call of their own, unlike Store.append() (which explicitly issues 'SET LOCAL search_path TO <tenant_schema>,public' inside its own transaction). Pool.acquire()'s applyRequestStorageRouting() derives the target schema from thread-local tenant_context - with no tenant set, it resolves to 'SET search_path TO public' only. Neither PartitionMaintenanceScheduler nor PartitionRetention is wired into src/main.zig or any other production entrypoint in this diff (confirmed via grep - zero call sites of runDailyLoop/runMaintenanceCycle/runArchivalAging/runEphemeralDrop outside their own files and tests), and neither performs its own per-tenant-schema fanout loop, so as shipped these jobs cannot reach any per-tenant events/events_ephemeral data at all when eventually wired up against more than one tenant schema - they would silently only ever operate against whichever single schema (or public, if none) the calling context happens to have set. This is NOT a regression this diff introduces: the pre-existing SCH-02 Scheduler.pollDueTimers() (src/scheduler/scheduler.zig, not touched by this diff) has the structurally identical gap against the equally PER_TENANT 'timers' table, and is also unwired from main.zig in this snapshot - this is an established, pre-existing pattern in this codebase's background-job architecture, not a new tenant-isolation violation unique to PAR-01..04. No test in par02_partition_catalog_test.zig or par03_retention_class_test.zig exercises more than one tenant schema (TestHarness.init() always sets DEFAULT_TENANT_ID), so this gap is untested but also undocumented as an accepted limitation in either design doc (src/design/par-02-partition-maintenance-job.md, src/design/par-03-partition-scoped-retention.md do not discuss multi-tenant fanout). Recommend filing as a follow-up issue (multi-tenant fanout wiring for PAR-02/PAR-03 and the pre-existing SCH-02 gap) rather than blocking this PASS, since: (a) it does not cause cross-tenant data exposure (worst case is these jobs silently do nothing for un-fanned-out tenants, not that they touch the wrong tenant's data), (b) it matches pre-existing SCH-02 precedent unchanged by this diff, and (c) neither job is wired into any running entrypoint yet in this batch.

SEPARATE NON-BLOCKING OBSERVATION (functional, not security): a delete-class event (routed to events_ephemeral) with payload >4096 bytes would have its event_payload_store INSERT (store.zig:645-658) rejected by that table's FK '(event_id, created_at) REFERENCES events(event_id, created_at)', which does not cover events_ephemeral rows - this fails safe via ROLLBACK/TransactionFailed (no data corruption, no cross-tenant leak) but is an untested functional gap, not covered by any of the 8 security invariants. Recommend a follow-up test/fix, not a security-gate blocker.

issues.description: PartitionMaintenanceScheduler/PartitionRetention (src/scheduler/partition_maintenance.zig, src/scheduler/partition_retention.zig) acquire pool connections without setting tenant_context, so as shipped they only ever operate against a single (or no) tenant schema and have no per-tenant fanout loop. Matches pre-existing SCH-02 Scheduler.pollDueTimers() precedent (not touched by this diff) rather than being a new regression. Neither job is wired into main.zig yet. Recommend a follow-up issue for multi-tenant fanout wiring before either job is put into production scheduling.

event_payload_store's FK only references events(event_id, created_at), not events_ephemeral. A delete-class event with payload >4096 bytes routed to events_ephemeral would hit an FK violation on its large-payload side-table INSERT and roll back (TransactionFailed) - fails safe, not a security defect, but untested and undocumented. Functional follow-up recommended.
